findings.title: Unguarded privileged writer: _grant reachable via handOver
findings.evidence_cypher: MATCH p = (e:Function {is_entry: true, guarded: false})-[:CALLS*1..6]->(t:Function {id: $id}) WITH p, length(p) AS len RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | n.id] AS path ORDER BY len LIMIT 3
findings.explanation: Treasury._grant(address) writes the privileged owner state variable and is reachable from the unguarded entry Treasury.handOver(address). Any caller can therefore grant ownership to an arbitrary address.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an onlyOwner access control modifier to Treasury.handOver(address) so only the current owner can call _grant.

findings.title: Unguarded privileged writer: setOwner
findings.evidence_cypher: MATCH p = (e:Function {is_entry: true, guarded: false})-[:CALLS*1..6]->(t:Function {id: $id}) WITH p, length(p) AS len RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | n.id] AS path ORDER BY len LIMIT 3
findings.explanation: Treasury.setOwner(address) directly writes the owner state variable and is itself an unguarded entry point. Any external caller can therefore take over ownership of the contract.
findings.recommended_fix: Add an onlyOwner access control modifier to Treasury.setOwner(address).

findings.title: Reentrancy in withdraw
findings.evidence_cypher: MATCH p = (e:Function {is_entry: true, guarded: false})-[:CALLS*1..6]->(t:Function {id: $id}) WITH p, length(p) AS len RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | n.id] AS path ORDER BY len LIMIT 3
findings.explanation: Treasury.withdraw(uint256) is an unguarded entry that performs an external ETH transfer before updating state, allowing a malicious recipient to reenter. This can drain the treasury balance.
findings.recommended_fix: Apply the checks-effects-interactions pattern by updating state before the external ETH call.

findings.title: Unchecked low-level call in refund
findings.evidence_cypher: MATCH p = (e:Function {is_entry: true, guarded: false})-[:CALLS*1..6]->(t:Function {id: $id}) WITH p, length(p) AS len RETURN [n IN nodes(p) | n.id] AS path ORDER BY len LIMIT 3
findings.explanation: Treasury.refund(uint256) is an unguarded entry that performs a low-level call without checking its return value. A failed transfer is silently ignored, leaving funds stuck or state inconsistent.
findings.recommended_fix: Check the success return value of the low-level call and revert on failure.
